uncited: Method-Specific Training Configurations specify the hyperparameters, optimization loops, and architectural adjustments required to train specific Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) variants [S18780-multi-scale-and-mip-aware-representations.md].

This family provides the concrete numerical values, loss functions, and network structures unique to each variant, distinguishing it from generic procedural steps like [Training Loop Setup](1522-training-loop-setup.md) or [Learning Rate Scheduling](2701-learning-rate-scheduling.md).

The methods in this family share the fundamental goal of minimizing the photometric error between rendered images and ground truth inputs via gradient descent [S18780-multi-scale-and-mip-aware-representations.md].
All methods utilize differentiable volume rendering to compute gradients with respect to the neural network parameters [S18780-multi-scale-and-mip-aware-representations.md].

Common structural elements include the use of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to map spatial coordinates and viewing directions to density and color, and the use of ray sampling strategies to query these networks [S18780-multi-scale-and-mip-aware-representations.md].

However, the specific activation functions, sampling densities, loss formulations, and optimizer settings vary significantly to address artifacts like aliasing, dark pixels, or memory constraints [S18780-multi-scale-and-mip-aware-representations.md].
For the Blender dataset, near/far thresholds are $t_n=2.0, t_f=6.0$.
Camera optimizer, appearance embedding, distortion loss, and scene contraction are disabled.
For LLFF, camera optimizer, appearance embedding, and distortion loss are disabled.
Batch size is 1024 rays during training and 2048 during evaluation.
The original NeRF paper established the baseline training configuration, which has been adapted for various datasets (Blender, LLFF) and variants (Mip-NeRF, DONeRF, etc.).
Subsequent works introduced specific optimizations to address issues like aliasing (Mip-NeRF), computational cost (DONeRF), defocus (AR-NeRF), and memory constraints (DP-based Selector).

The field has evolved from simple MLP-based NeRFs to more complex architectures involving hash encodings (Instant-NGP, Neuralangelo) and GAN-based frameworks (StyleNeRF, AR-NeRF), each requiring tailored training configurations.
